site: any employer on Phenom People's careers widget, confirmed on ADT Careers (jobs.adt.com)
class: A page classifier whose every rule for 'this is an account/registration step' assumes a password field exists, so a genuinely passwordless registration gate is read as not-an-account-page and falls to generic form filling
symptom: ADT Careers' application stopped with 'the application form bounced back to the job posting' after the circuit breaker caught 3 identical attempts, with no mention of the actual blocker.
root_cause: The page was Phenom People's 'Authentication screen. You don't need to have an account': just an email box, a honeypot, and a required 'I agree with the terms and conditions' checkbox, then Next -- no password field anywhere. account_state.read_state() classifies every account/registration state from the number of password boxes (CREATE_FORM needs >=1, SIGN_IN_FORM needs ==1, EMAIL_FIRST needs 'Sign In' wording); zero passwords and no sign-in wording fell through every rule to NONE, so the page was never routed to browser_automation.handle_auth_gate at all. Generic page_agent filling correctly left the T&C checkbox unticked (safety.is_attestation) but had no reason to withhold Next, clicked it anyway, and the site's own client-side validation bounced the page back -- 3 times, until the fingerprint-based circuit breaker (CLAUDE.md Sec 6) stopped the run with its generic message. Even with classification fixed, handle_auth_gate and fill_create_account_form independently re-derived the same password-count assumption and would have bailed again before reaching the checkbox logic that already correctly holds a terms-and-conditions box for the candidate (BEHAVIOUR.md, 'Creating an account').
why_tests_missed: Every existing account_state.py and fill_create_account_form test fixture has at least one password field (a Create Account form, a Sign In form, or an EMAIL_FIRST sign-in-first page); none modeled a registration gate that never asks for a password at all, so the zero-password path through both the classifier and the form filler was never exercised.
fix: account_state.read_state() gained a pattern for this wording ('you don't need an account', 'get started ... using your email') that classifies a zero-password page with an email box as CREATE_FORM instead of NONE. browser_automation.handle_auth_gate's pw_count==0 branch now routes to fill_create_account_form (guarded by account_on_record()) instead of returning False immediately. fill_create_account_form's entry guard, password-typing/reconfirmation steps, and its Next/Continue button fallback are now conditional on pw_fields being non-empty instead of assuming at least one password box; the checkbox-holding logic itself (is_attestation, is_account_creation_consent) needed no change -- it already does the right thing once the page reaches it.
prevention: A new project's account/registration-step classifier and form filler should treat 'how many password fields' as one signal among several, never a gate that a genuinely passwordless flow cannot pass at all -- test at least one zero-password registration fixture from the start, alongside the create/sign-in/email-first ones.
